clue.text: Crazily scream 'It's myrrh!' as a festive greeting

indicators.note: acting crazily, the letters of the quoted scream are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone shrieks about myrrh, of all things, as their way of wishing everyone well for the season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crazily' rearranges SCREAM plus ITSMYRRH, fourteen letters in all; 'as a' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: The standard spoken wish exchanged on 25 December is a festive greeting.

clue.text: Leader of reindeer facing terrible hold-up?

definitions.text: Leader of reindeer facing terrible hold-up?

indicators.note: one piece faces, so sits in front of, the next
the leader of a word is its opening letter, here of reindeer
a terrible thing is a mess, so the letters of hold-up are jumbled

explanation.surface: The front reindeer is up against a dreadful delay on Christmas Eve.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: in the song, the red-nosed reindeer leads the sleigh when fog threatens to hold up Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: In the song, the red-nosed reindeer guides the sleigh, so he heads the team when a foggy delay threatens.

clue.text: Thou shalt broadcast, Noel!

indicators.note: broadcast means put out over the air, so the words are spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: old-fashioned 'thou shalt' means 'you will', contracted to you'll

explanation.surface: A biblical-sounding command addressed to someone named Noel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noel' looks like a man's name being addressed; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel and this old word are both names for the Christmas season.

clue.text: Musical group that keeps things tidy on top?

definitions.meaning: a big-haired rock group of the 1980s glam-metal style

definitions.text: that keeps things tidy on top?
definitions.meaning: an elastic loop or headband holding the hair in place on the head

explanation.surface: A band whose job is keeping things neat at the top.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a glam-rock outfit famous for its hairstyles; the other is an accessory that holds the hair back.

clue.text: Son leaves somewhere cold for somewhere warmer

indicators.note: the son leaves, so his letter departs from the cold place

parts.note: Siberia is the famously freezing region of Russia

explanation.surface: A young man quits a frozen place to head for the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish-Portuguese peninsula is a hot region far milder than northern Russia.

clue.text: A lucky bit of 11?

parts.note: 11 is the Christmas pudding, into which an old silver coin was stirred for luck

explanation.walkthrough: The old British three-penny coin (a 'bit') was hidden in the Christmas pudding; whoever found it had good luck.
explanation.definitionFit: The pre-decimal coin was traditionally the lucky charm baked into the Christmas pudding.

clue.text: Praise grown-up getting to grips with a charade at last

indicators.note: to get to grips with is to grab hold, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: a grown-up is an adult

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of charade

explanation.surface: Congratulating a grown-up who finally masters a game of charades.
explanation.definitionFit: To adulate is to flatter or praise excessively.

clue.text: Star with allowance for party

parts.note: a star is a celebrity, shortened to celeb
a ration is a fixed allowance

explanation.surface: A famous person brings their allotted amount to a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A party is a festive gathering held to mark an occasion.

clue.text: Answer Rodney's brother and assistant: cook turkey on the barbie here?

definitions.text: cook turkey on the barbie here?

parts.note: Del Boy is Rodney's older brother in the British sitcom Only Fools and Horses
an aide is an assistant

explanation.surface: Clues about a sitcom family lead to a festive barbecue down under.
explanation.walkthrough: Only Fools and Horses is a British TV comedy about two market-trading brothers. The city is in Australia, where Christmas falls in summer.
explanation.definitionFit: Christmas in this South Australian city comes in summer, so turkey on the barbecue is plausible.

clue.text: Wake up party animal to receive seconds

indicators.note: to receive is to take in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a roué is a dissolute pleasure-seeker, a party animal

explanation.surface: Rouse a reveller so they can have second helpings.
explanation.definitionFit: To rouse someone is to wake them from sleep.

clue.text: Papa surprisingly muddling up what's served with brandy sauce

parts.note: P is Papa in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests the letters land in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Dad unexpectedly confuses the Christmas dinner order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'muddling up' looks like the anagram signal but is the fodder; 'surprisingly' does the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional British Christmas dessert is served with brandy sauce or brandy butter.

clue.text: Sing happily till drunk

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so the letters of till lurch into a new order

explanation.surface: Keep singing merrily until you are intoxicated.
explanation.definitionFit: To lilt is to sing or speak with a cheerful rising and falling rhythm.

clue.text: Get rid of nameless relation playing around with Bet

indicators.note: playing around with things mixes them up, so the letters are reshuffled
without its name, the word loses N, the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: An anonymous relative fooling around with a woman named Bet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nameless' works on the word itself: it strips the abbreviation for name, not a person's name, before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: To obliterate is to wipe out or destroy completely, to get rid of.

clue.text: Showing anger, aggrieve oddball eating just the outer parts of sprouts

indicators.note: eating takes something in, so one piece goes inside the other
oddball means eccentric or weird, so the letters of aggrieve are made odd
only the first and last letters of sprouts are used

explanation.surface: An oddball nibbles only the outer leaves of sprouts and gets cross.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aggrieve' looks like a near-miss spelling of the answer, but it is the anagram fodder for 'oddball', which is the signal, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone aggressive is hostile and combative, displaying anger.

clue.text: Dodgy Hogmanay tree

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or not right, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A questionable New Year's Eve tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Hogmanay is the Scottish name for New Year's Eve and its celebrations.
explanation.definitionFit: This tropical hardwood is a tree prized for reddish-brown timber.

clue.text: Possibly meet men to follow shooting star?

indicators.note: the men follow, so they come after
possibly offers one possible arrangement of the letters of meet

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers or men

explanation.surface: Perhaps meeting people who want to follow a falling star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shooting' looks like the anagram signal but belongs to the definition; 'Possibly' does the rearranging. Other ranks is the army term for soldiers who are not officers.
explanation.definitionFit: A streak of light from space debris burning up is commonly called a shooting star.

clue.text: Cut up good English Xmas treat

parts.note: to mince is to cut up finely
PI, short for pious, means good

explanation.surface: Chop up a fine British Christmas delicacy.
explanation.definitionFit: The small fruit-filled pastry is a traditional Christmas sweet.

clue.text: Doubtful Queen will return after occasionally funny slur

indicators.note: the queen comes after the other piece
only now and then, so every other letter of the words is taken
returning means going back, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Not sure whether the monarch will come back after an odd joke-insult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes the even letters of 'funny slur', UNSU; 'will return' turns ER to RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Doubtful and this word both mean lacking certainty.

clue.text: One troubled by the past, present and future?

definitions.text: One troubled by the past, present and future?

parts.words: One troubled by the past, present and future
parts.note: in Dickens's A Christmas Carol, the miser is visited by the Ghosts of Christmas Past, Present and Yet to Come

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as general anxiety about time; it means three Christmas ghosts.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's miser in A Christmas Carol is haunted by three spirits of Christmas times.

clue.text: Very late collection for a seasonal service

parts.note: the middle of the night is very late
a mass is a large collection or heap

explanation.surface: A very late church collection at a Christmas service.
explanation.definitionFit: The Christmas Eve Eucharist held at twelve o'clock is a seasonal church service.

clue.text: Female relative that is stealing gift, ultimately: it's hard

parts.note: gran is a grandmother

indicators.note: to steal is to take, so one piece takes in another

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of gift

explanation.surface: Grandma, that is, nicks a present, which is tough.
explanation.definitionFit: This igneous rock is a byword for hardness.

clue.text: Trio travelling to take in Eastern newborn, initially — from here?

indicators.note: taking in means enclosing, so one piece goes inside
travelling suggests movement, so the letters of trio move around
initially points to the first letter of newborn

explanation.surface: Three travellers set out to see an Eastern newborn: the Magi visiting Jesus.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the surface: the three wise men came from the East, which is where 'here' points.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magi of the carol came 'from the East'; the old poetic word for the East names where they set out.

clue.text: Remove limitations on Germany and Spain regarding 75% of Strictly

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)
re means regarding or concerning

indicators.note: three quarters of the eight-letter word, its first six letters

explanation.surface: European dance contestants are judged on most of Strictly Come Dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly Come Dancing is a popular British TV ballroom contest.
explanation.definitionFit: To derestrict is to lift controls, especially a speed limit, so it means removing limitations.

clue.text: Slump over dessert?

parts.note: to slump is to sag
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Collapsing over the pudding course.
explanation.definitionFit: Sago pudding is a milky dessert made from palm starch, hence the question mark.

clue.text: See 20
Complain about one girl

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: to moan is to complain
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Grumbling about a particular young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A biblical female name, so an example of a girl's name.

clue.text: Stress most of hamper upset little sister

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged
most of the word loses its last letter

parts.note: sis is a familiar short form of sister

explanation.surface: Your baby sister is upset by most of the Christmas hamper, causing stress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims HAMPER to HAMPE; 'upset' rearranges it to EMPHA.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphasis is stress laid on a word or point.

clue.text: Sozzled sellers sense stocking books could show persistence

indicators.note: stocking means holding in stock, so the books go inside
sozzled means drunk, so the letters reel into a new order

parts.note: NT, the New Testament, is a set of books

explanation.surface: Drunk booksellers keep stocking titles out of sheer doggedness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sellers sense' gives twelve of the fourteen letters; the books are the New Testament, slipped into the jumble. 'could show' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: Relentlessness is unyielding determination, which is a form of persistence.
